verified: The 300 products are real catalog rows from Open Food Facts, Open Beauty Facts and Open Products Facts, pulled on 2026-10-02 and published under the Open Database License.
Each product row is stored exactly as its source returned it. The checksum of the file is recorded in data/catalog_raw.meta.json.
A row with no name or no brand was left out: 66 rows, each listed in data/catalog_raw.meta.json.
All 280 of the 280 thirteen-digit barcodes in the catalog pass the GS1 check digit.
A change of declared net content requires a new barcode: GS1 GTIN Management Standard, rule "Declared net content" (https://www.gs1.org/1/gtinrules/en/rule/266/declared-net-content).
Every script is deterministic: the same seeds give the same files, byte for byte.
Every number on the replay page is counted from the files in data/ when the page loads.
assumed: 3 stores share one planogram of 300 products: 7 aisles, 4 shelves per aisle, shelf 1 at the bottom.
Products of one brand sit side by side: each aisle is ordered by brand, then by name.
A product gets 1, 2 or 3 facings, by how often it was scanned in its source catalog.
Every facing is 0.2 m wide. Aisles are 3 m apart. Shelf heights are 0.3, 0.7, 1.1, 1.5 m.
Out of stock: 2 to 3 positions per aisle are empty on day 1.
Misplaced: 1 to 2 single units per store sit in the wrong aisle, and stay there on every day.
Restocking: overnight after day 1, 50% of the empty positions are refilled, rounded down, and 1 to 2 stocked positions per store run out. Nothing changes after day 2.
3 full walks per store, one per day, each by a different badge, starting 2026-10-02: day 1 at 09:00 UTC and 1 m/s; day 2 at 14:30 UTC and 0.9 m/s; day 3 at 11:15 UTC and 1.1 m/s.
A walk is a serpentine: the first aisle forward, the next one back.
The camera takes 5 frames per second. Each stocked facing is read once per walk, in the frame taken closest to it. An empty facing gives no detection.
A detection's 3D position is the facing's true position plus noise of 0.03 m standard deviation per axis.
The bounding box is a flat projection onto a 3840 x 2160 frame, with no lens distortion.
The fields of a detection record are a guess at what a shelf-reading camera reports.
No image is used. image_ref names a frame that does not exist.
A label's text is the catalog row's brand, name and size joined together. Real labels differ more from their catalog rows, so matching is easier here than on real images.
The read text is damaged in four independent ways: a unit is respelled on 30% of reads, the text is cut short on 30%, 1 to 3 characters are lost on 35%, and the case changes on 40%.
A barcode is read on 15% of detections, and is never misread.
Confidence is highest for an undamaged read and falls with each kind of damage.
5% of detections are reported twice in the same frame, with a new id and the text read again.
A second badge walks one aisle of each store on day 1, 120 seconds after the first walk starts.
3% of frames are sent twice, unchanged.

Catalog v2 takes effect on day 2: 3 products renamed by a fixed rule, 2 given a size 10% smaller and a new barcode, 1 discontinued, and 1 real product added. The renames, the sizes and the new barcodes are simulated.
A simulated barcode keeps the first 7 digits of the barcode it replaces and carries a valid check digit.
From day 2 all stock of a resized product carries the new barcode. Stock of the discontinued product stays on the shelf with its old label. The planogram is not updated.
"Sold in the United States" is the sources' own tag. Some personal care and household rows are products made for other markets.
The replay page's opening view plays one aisle slower than the walk, and states by how much.
The replay page draws a repeated detection a quarter of a second after the first, and a re-sent row just after its walk ends: the data gives a re-sent row no arrival time.
